original.result: For ℓ different from char(k), the injective map Tℓ(A)→Tℓ(B) induced by an isogeny u:A→B has cokernel canonically isomorphic to ker(u)(k)[ℓ∞]. Thus integral invertibility is equivalent to ℓ not dividing deg(u). Milne I §7 and Lemma10.16 supply the divisibility statement. This prime-support criterion survives the correction of the minimal denominator in C-SA06-265.

original.result: The H¹-inverse requirement is exactly the (1,2n−1) Künneth condition for an integral universal zero-cycle: the induced endomorphism of Alb(X) is the identity by faithful H¹ realization. Voisin (2025), §2 before Lemma2.1 and Theorem1.4, gives a smooth projective complex threefold with representable CH0 and no such cycle. Alexandrou (2026), Theorem1.3, improves this to a surface with Alb(S)=E under the stated End(E) hypotheses. Thus the universal integral assertion is false, even under representability of CH0. A rational universal cycle exists; a rational point of the stated generic symmetric-power fibre remains a sufficient special hypothesis. See the complete integral correspondence proof in computation_notes.md.

Alexandrou (2026), Theorem1.3, improves this to a surface with Alb(S)=E under the stated End(E) hypotheses. Thus the universal integral assertion is false, even under representability of CH0. A rational universal cycle exists; a rational point of the stated generic symmetric-power fibre remains a sufficient special hypothesis. See the complete integral correspondence proof in computation_notes.md.

original.result: The universal assertion is false by a checked inference from primary results. Subtracting the two factor pushforwards times the zero sections removes the unmixed components of any proposed one-cycle integrally. The remaining component is ±c1(P)^{2g−1}/(2g−1)!, as the exterior-algebra calculation verifies. Beckmann–de Gaay Fortman2023 Thm1.1 then implies integral Hodge for one-cycles on A. Engel–de Gaay Fortman–Schreieder2025/2026 Thm1.1 disproves this for very general principally polarized complex A of dimension≥4. All integral cohomology groups of A are torsion-free.
